items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Lee Young, oh yeah. Norman had this unique way about him of getting people who he had great admiration for, or people who he considered to be the top jazz musicians of the day. His whole concept was to put unlikely combinations of musicians together and just let the sparks fly, as he would say. He got some interesting concerts recorded as a result of that. Oh, you have the article, there? Carolyn found the article that's about the April 6th event, and you can take a look at that. I will never forget that . . .…

in any case, we became very friendly. Norman once told me – and it's mentioned in this article that Carolyn’s found and Dave is reading now – that we were standing in the wings listening to another one of the acts. I had either performed or was about to perform. Norman and I were standing there together, and he said to me, "J.J., the only meaningful music is jam sessions and the blues. All other music is pure bullshit."
